clue.text: Friendly, minutes after fighting

indicators.note: after places the minutes letter behind the word for fighting

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: Someone turns friendly a few minutes after a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a friendly one; the two adjectives are synonyms for cordial manner.

clue.text: Reported playmaker over breach of rules, we hear, in some game

indicators.note: reported says the playwright's name is to be taken as it is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a playmaker is a writer of plays: Oscar Wilde

indicators.note: we hear marks the rule-breaking word as one taken by its sound, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: a breach of the rules in sport is a foul

explanation.surface: A sports report about a playmaker going over the line with a foul in some match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' looks like a sporting term but means a writer of plays, Oscar Wilde. 'Over' just joins the two pieces, one above the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and other birds shot for sport are game birds, collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Cheese that's fine with tea, oddly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: oddly says the letters of fine's abbreviation and the word tea are to be arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A cheese that goes nicely with a cup of tea, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take odd letters of 'tea', but here it shuffles F plus TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Modern erection badly constructed

indicators.note: something badly constructed has its parts put together wrongly, so the word erection is to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A modern building that has been badly put up.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare word means recent or newfangled, a learned synonym for modern.

clue.text: Revered a party on the far left

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
red stands for the political far left, communists and socialists

explanation.surface: A party on the extreme left was greatly revered.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to revere or worship them, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Military vehicle endlessly seen in adorable Indian town

indicators.note: seen in places the shortened vehicle inside the word for adorable

parts.note: darling, as an adjective, means adorable or sweet

indicators.note: endlessly says the vehicle loses its final letter

parts.note: a jeep is a military vehicle

explanation.surface: A jeep spotted in a charming town in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the vehicle's last letter, and 'seen in' puts the rest inside the word for adorable; the town gives its name to a famous tea, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hill town in West Bengal, famous for the tea grown around it.

clue.text: Scene of historic 21 and game of cards

definitions.meaning: the American city where colonists dumped British tea into the harbour in 1773
a whist-like card game of the eighteenth century bears the same name as the city

explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the TEA PARTY, so the scene is the city of that famous protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts city hosted the 1773 tea protest and also gave its name to a card game.

clue.text: Poet's pronouncement is dismal

indicators.note: pronouncement says the poet's surname is to be taken as it is spoken, giving another spelling

parts.note: the poet is Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A poet declares that things are gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Poet's' joins the name to 'pronouncement': the poet's name as said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey day is a dull, cheerless one, so the colour means dismal.

clue.text: Girl band from town down under

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, as in Lewis Carroll's heroine
a hairband worn across the top of the head, named after Carroll's heroine
a short name for ... Springs, a town in the middle of Australia

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings in a row; 'from' just links them. 'Down under' is Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a girl's name, a kind of hairband and Australians' short name for Alice Springs.

clue.text: Effort finally revealed name of top solver on TV

definitions.meaning: an attempt or effort, as in a noble undertaking

definitions.text: finally revealed name of top solver on TV
definitions.meaning: Inspector Morse's first name, kept secret until late in the stories

explanation.walkthrough: The TV detective Morse famously hid his first name; it was revealed only near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a strenuous attempt, and it was also detective Morse's long-hidden first name.

clue.text: Eccentric that appears in strange dream

indicators.note: strange says the letters of the following words are to be arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar character turns up in a weird dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appears in' just links the definition to the wordplay. Carroll's hatter is the eccentric host of the 21 (TEA PARTY).
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's hat-maker in Wonderland is a byword for a wildly eccentric person.

clue.text: Like black stone in pier

definitions.meaning: jet is a hard black stone, so like jet means jet-black
a landing stage or pier projecting into water

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means jet-like, and the noun names a landing pier, two unrelated senses of one spelling.

clue.text: Not this piece for piano, therefore

indicators.note: a piece of the following words means the letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Not this musical piece for piano, therefore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' links the indicator to the words: the run sits across 'piano' and 'therefore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for one more different item means not this one but a different one.

clue.text: A state in East briefly upset another state in East

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read from bottom to top
briefly says the state is cut to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: Massachusetts is a state in the eastern US

explanation.surface: An eastern American state, upset, gives way to another eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts the state to MASS, which 'upset' turns to SSAM after A. The answer is in north-east India, another East entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state of north-east India, famous for its tea gardens.

clue.text: Capital mostly invested in male dominion, in which people don't have faith

definitions.text: in which people don't have faith

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money placed in a business

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
dom is a suffix meaning dominion, as in kingdom

indicators.note: mostly says the capital loses its last letter

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: Money from the capital is mostly invested in a male-run realm of unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the capital's last letter, and 'invested in' sounds financial but just means placed inside. 'Dom' is the suffix of kingdom and Christendom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the world of heathens, the realm or state where there is no religious belief.

clue.text: Girl turned in fees for foreign governesses

indicators.note: in places the reversed name inside the word for fees

parts.note: dues are fees paid, as for membership

indicators.note: turned says the girl's name is to be read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl turned up in the bill for some foreign governesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses the girl's name and 'in' places it within the fees; 'for' only links the definition, and 'foreign' points to these Spanish chaperones.
explanation.definitionFit: These are older women in Spain or Portugal who act as chaperones or governesses to girls.

clue.text: A rash plan I crazily formulated, as leader of 21

indicators.note: crazily formulated says the letters of the preceding words are to be put together wildly

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a mad scheme they cooked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the TEA PARTY, the US anti-government movement; 'as' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Alaska governor was a figurehead of the American Tea Party movement.

clue.text: Dancing line seen in South America repeatedly

indicators.note: seen in places the line letter inside the doubled abbreviation
repeatedly says the abbreviation for the continent is written twice

explanation.surface: A dance line is seen again and again in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: SA doubled is SASA, and L goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a Latin American dance and the dancing done to it.

clue.text: 6, 13 down, 23, 29 8, or 30 that's repeatedly found in dance

definitions.meaning: the cross-referenced answers are all varieties of tea, and this word is slang for tea
said twice, it names a Latin American ballroom dance

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are DARJEELING, ASSAM, OOLONG, EARL GREY and GUNPOWDER, all teas. 'That's' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for tea, and doubled it names a Latin dance.

clue.text: A doctor's carrying present for those who follow

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, and the possessive gives an S
here means present, as in answering a roll call

explanation.surface: A doctor's carrying a present for the followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'doctor's' supplies a plural letter; 'carrying' means holding inside, and 'present' is the roll-call reply, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: People who adhere to a cause or leader are its followers.

clue.text: Put into ground, using section of main terrace

indicators.note: a section of the following words means a stretch of their letters taken from within

explanation.surface: Burying something using part of the main terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body in a grave is to place it in the ground, a formal verb.

clue.text: Anti-government group still rising, securing a role

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: still means yet, as in still to come
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An anti-government group is still on the rise and has landed a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns YET into TEY, which holds A + PART.
explanation.definitionFit: The US conservative movement, named after the 1773 Boston protest, opposes big government.

clue.text: Hormone change can make one rail

indicators.note: change says the letters of the word hormone are to be altered in order

explanation.surface: A change of hormones can turn someone into a complaining person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a verb meaning complain, but it is a family of wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This small black water bird belongs to the rail family of marsh birds.

clue.text: Export from China needing to be cut, top-sliced

indicators.note: top-sliced means the first letter is removed

parts.note: something too long needs to be cut down

explanation.surface: A Chinese export that needs trimming, with its top sliced off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-sliced' removes the T from TOO LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dark Chinese tea, part-fermented, sold abroad as an export.

clue.text: People who are unsettled and crazy in limited numbers

indicators.note: in places the word for crazy inside the shortened numbers

parts.note: NOS is the shortened, or limited, form of numbers
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Unsettled people who go crazy in small numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' shortens 'numbers' to the abbreviation NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers who have no fixed home are people who never settle in one place.

clue.text: How gas gets mixed with hydrogen? Rubbish!

indicators.note: gets mixed says the letters of how gas are to be stirred together

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about mixing gas with hydrogen, met with a dismissive cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins H on after the shuffled HOWGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This word for nonsense means worthless talk, originally swill fed to pigs.

clue.text: See 16
Young male worker's mature under pressure

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the word for mature beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A young lad at work matures under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'worker's' stands for 'is' and links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy employed to run errands in a hotel or for a noble is a page.

clue.text: Move quickly to follow protest, as member of 21

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for moving quickly after the protest

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Hurrying to join a protest as a member of a political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the TEA PARTY, here the Mad Hatter's in Wonderland; 'as' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This mad animal is one of the guests at the tea party in Carroll's Wonderland.

clue.text: Tea-maker possibly used by Father Brown

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Chesterton's priest-detective brews something for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Brown' looks like the detective, but it only supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint or camomile steeped in hot water makes a herbal infusion, so such a plant may make tea.

clue.text: Disraeli, for example, showing ability to listen to Liberal

parts.note: an ear for something is an ability to listen or hear well
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, the political party

explanation.surface: The Tory Disraeli shows he will listen to a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' links the definition. Disraeli became Earl of Beaconsfield; with 8 this gives EARL GREY tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was made Earl of Beaconsfield in 1876, so he is an example of this peer.

clue.text: Explosive editor held back by grown-up when drunk

indicators.note: held, as a captive is held, means the editor's letters are kept captive within the drunk grown-up's letters
when drunk says the letters of grown-up are to be jumbled, as a drunk staggers
back says the editor's abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An explosive editor is restrained by a drunken adult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the editor, 'held' puts that inside GUNPOWR (the anagram of GROWNUP from 'when drunk'), and 'by' links. The answer is also a green tea, matching the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The black powder used in guns and fireworks is an explosive; it also names a green tea.

clue.text: Appraiser backed raise over time

indicators.note: over means covering, so the reversed word sits round the time letter
backed says the word for raise is read in reverse

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as children or livestock

explanation.surface: An appraiser backed a pay rise over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' turns REAR into RAER, which goes over T.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rates or assesses value is an appraiser of things.
